name: Chicken and Sweetcorn Soup
description: Creamed corn and shredded chicken bound in a silky egg-thickened broth, a Cantonese takeaway staple worldwide.
ingredients: a handful of fresh scallion greens, chopped
instructions: Heat neutral vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the sliced scallion whites and grated fresh ginger gently until soft and fragrant.
Stir in the five-spice powder and white pepper, toasting briefly until the kitchen fills with their aroma.
Add the whole duck and bok choy, stirring well to coat everything in the spiced base.
Pour in the water, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot, and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat, cover, and let everything simmer gently until the whole duck is tender, about 15 mins.
Stir in the egg noodles and continue simmering for a few minutes more, until heated through.
tips: Taste and adjust the seasoning right at the end — the water reduces as it simmers, concentrating the flavor.
Skim off any foam that rises during the first few minutes of simmering for a clearer, cleaner broth.
Letting the pot rest for 10 minutes off the heat allows the flavors to deepen before serving.
